messages:
SecurityBot: Alert: unusual S3 ACL change detected by CloudTrail for bucket `redwood-logs-prod` from IP 3.14.159.26 at 2025-11-04T14:12:03Z. Event: PutBucketAcl. Severity: HIGH :rotating_light:
Alex R.: saw that, good catch. can someone confirm whether that ACL made the bucket public? :eyes:
Maria S.: checking now — `aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-logs-prod` returns `Grantee: AllUsers` on WRITE? looking at the event payload in CloudTrail.
Jason: if it's AllUsers we need containment now. Steps: 1) remove public ACL 2) revoke any active session tokens used 3) rotate offending access keys 4) lock down IAM role.
Katie: running containment: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-logs-prod --acl private` -> applying. will post exit code.
Katie: DONE exit code 0. bucket ACL set to private. :white_check_mark:
SRE-Ops: adding temporary block rule on the bucket in the infra layer too (s3 block public access) with IaC patch. pushing a TF change to patch branch now. PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/5421
Alex R.: good. Maria, can you find which principal made the PutBucketAcl? need user/role and associated access key/session.
Maria S.: CloudTrail shows `userIdentity.type = AWSAccount` then `assumedRole` with sessionName `ci-deploy-role/session-abc123`. Source IP matches an external CI runner. `aws sts decode-authorization-message` indicates it was a federated session.
Jason: sounds like the CI role had an overly broad permission schema. Policy snippet: `{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"*"}`. We should narrow to specific buckets.
Dave: I'm revoking the active sessions for `ci-deploy-role`. Command: `aws sts revoke-session --session-id session-abc123` (note: we used our internal tooling to kill the session). session killed. :lock:
Katie: rotating keys used by the CI runner now — updating secrets in internal vault and triggering CI redeploy to pick up new creds. Secrets path: `vault/ci/redwood-deploy`.
Maria S.: Audit note: CloudTrail shows `GetObject` 120 requests between 14:12 and 14:18. Looks like a scripted download of logs. We need to assume exfiltration. Exporting the event logs to the incident bucket `redwood-incident-archive`.
Alex R.: Communications: security@redwood and affected product owners notified. Legal looped in (cc @katie). We'll treat as PII candidate until proven otherwise.
SRE-Ops: short-term mitigation PR merged and applied: IAM policy tightened for `ci-deploy-role` to only `s3:GetObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::redwood-artifacts/*`. Also added `Condition: StringEquals:aws:SourceIp` to restrict CI runner IP ranges.
Jason: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) enforce org SCP that denies `s3:PutBucketAcl` for non-admin roles 2) add automated CI preflight that runs `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` on any role that gets new permissions 3) enable S3 Object Lock and Inventory on prod buckets 4) KMS: rotate CMK used to encrypt logs and ensure key policy disallows cross-account decrypts.
Maria S.: I opened incident ticket INC-2025-1124 and attached CloudTrail export + list of object keys downloaded. Adding timeline and remediation steps.
Alex R.: can someone own the post-incident action items? I can take IAM policy/SCP. Maria can own audit + timeline. Jason takes CI gating and preflight automation. SRE-Ops will handle infra patching and monitoring.
Katie: quick config checklist we should add to onboarding: `S3 block-public-access` enabled, least-privilege role templates, require key rotation every 90 days, enable KMS key rotation on CMKs. I'll add to infra checklist.
Dave: we should also enable alerting for `PutBucketAcl` and `PutBucketPolicy` in the SIEM with higher priority and automated containment runbook. Opening a ticket for detection tuning.
Alex R.: thanks team. Postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 PT. I'll draft a short status to execs now. :wave:
SecurityBot: Incident INC-2025-1124 created, severity HIGH, assigned to eng-security. More updates will be appended here.
